$CRWV is down 15% today and Wall Street wants you to think it's because of this podcast!!

1) first of all, this D.A. Davidson's Gil Luria guy went on Prof G and said "the equity value is going to be zero." Mind you, his price target on the company is $100. This isn't new for him. In January he upgraded $CRWV from Underperform to Neutral and nearly doubled his target, from $36 to $68, in the same note where he wrote that the equity "could ultimately become worthless." He called the upgrade "tactical." So you're told the stock is worth zero and you're told to hold it at the same time. That isn't research at all. It's hedging your career, just in case something goes wrong. Which again goes back to my point that the sell side are a bunch of complete clowns and have no conviction in anything. 

2) the real signal came yesterday, and it came from credit, not equity as Luria said it did. CoreWeave's 2032 bonds touched a 15% yield intraday and closed at a record 14.5%. For context, CoreWeave sold 2031 notes at 9.75% in April. In six months the market has repriced its debt by almost 500bp. The stock is just catching up to what bond investors already said.

3) But ppl keep forgetting that CoreWeave is the cleanest bet on AI compute, even as it’s the most leveraged one:

- $130bn of contracted backlog
- three straight financing deals in recent months, including a $3bn convertible and a $1.1bn junk bond for a data center project
- GPUs bought with debt, rented out under multi year contracts

So the bull and bear cases are the same sentence. If the AI build out continues (which I think it’s going to and actually accelerate) that backlog turns into cash and the debt gets paid. If it stalls, the shareholders sit behind the bondholders.

What the Street keeps missing imo is that demand isn't the question. Every hyperscaler, every lab and every memory maker is telling you compute is sold out through 2027. The question is the cost of money. A 14.5% yield on a company with $104bn of backlog isn't the market pricing a CRWV going bankrupt. It’s just the market pricing fear of refinancing…which Jensen had already put out an MOU two months ago with the biggest banks on Wall Street asking for $500B. I mean come on, how fast did we forget that???
